title: Add sampled-affinity-calibrator and contextual-release-drafter
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: onboarding a growing set of model variants uncovered gaps in a) how representative performance samples are chosen for profile calibration and b) how changelogs capture context tied to sample regressions. This PR introduces two complementary components: a Sampled Affinity Calibrator (SAC) which creates affinity-weighted sample buckets per model variant and workload slice, and a Contextual Release Drafter (CRD) which synthesizes concise release notes tied to representative sample traces and performance deltas.

What this changes (high level): adds an offline calibration pipeline that takes telemetry + small probe workloads and outputs a per-variant affinity vector used to bias sampling for ongoing profiling; extends the model registry release pipeline with a drafter that attaches contextual bullets to autogenerated changelogs (examples include top-3 regressions, representative prompt, and suggested mitigation knobs).

Key goals: reduce noisy profile drift by ensuring sampled calibration sets better reflect served request distributions, and produce changelogs that are actionable for runtime/config teams and SREs.

Implementation notes: single-string description of code changes and behaviour. The SAC is implemented as a new service under registry/pipeline/sac with a compact estimator that fits into existing on-boarding flows. It outputs a small JSON affinity vector per model-version (kept in registry metadata). The CRD hooks into release-assembler and consumes: model profile deltas, a small set of representative prompts (sampled according to SAC), and evaluation metrics to render 3-5 bullet release notes and a short human-readable rationale. Both components are opt-in via onboard flags and default to safe fallbacks (uniform sampling; legacy changelog path) when not enabled.

Checklist (user-visible):
- [x] Add SAC offline pipeline and unit tests.
- [x] Persist affinity vectors into model metadata with version stamps.
- [x] CRD produces stable, reproducible draft text stored alongside release drafts.
- [x] Backwards-compatible: existing onboard flows unaffected when feature flags off.
- [x] Integration tests that run small probe workloads in CI and validate draft output shape.

Commits (summary):
- 9a7b2d1: introduce SAC estimator and CLI orchestrator (sac/estimator.go, sac/cli.py).
- b3c4ef0: add registry schema extension for affinity vectors and migration script (migrations/20241108_add_affinity_column.sql).
- f2d1a88: CRD module, templates, and release-assembler integration (release/crd/).
- 40cde7b: tests: unit + integration harness that simulates probe traffic and asserts stable drafts.
- 5ac3f11: docs: onboarding guide updates and examples (docs/model-onboard/sac-crd.md).

Files changed (high-level):
- registry/pipeline/sac/estimator.go
- registry/pipeline/sac/cli.py
- migrations/20241108_add_affinity_column.sql
- registry/storage/metadata_v2.go (schema + read/write hooks)
- release/crd/drafter.py and templates/release_bullets.mustache
- tests/integration/test_sac_crd_end2end.py
- docs/model-onboard/sac-crd.md
- ci/workflows/sac-crd-integration.yml

Testing and CI: new CI workflow (sac-crd-integration) that runs the small probe harness (fast, ~3m) and ensures no regressions in draft generation. Standard unit tests added; coverage threshold maintained. Initial runs showed a flaky test that was fixed by increasing probe-seed determinism. Final CI status: all checks passed on final push.

Backward compatibility and migration: added a lightweight migration that backfills a default uniform affinity vector for existing versions; rollout plan includes an A/B compare window where SAC-derived sampling is evaluated against uniform sampling for two weeks before full opt-in. No breaking schema changes.

Performance notes: estimator runs offline and adds negligible latency to onboarding; affinity vectors are small (typically 8-16 floats) stored as compressed base64 metadata. CRD is pure offline text generation (uses cached evaluation outputs) and does not affect serving runtime.

Review summary and conversation: the review thread below is condensed into a single string.
- Priya Singh (reviewer): "Overall design looks good. Two asks: please add audit logs for affinity writes and include a TTL for stored sample seeds."
- Maya Chen (author): "Added audit log hooks in registry/storage/metadata_v2.go and introduced seed_ttl config; updated tests to cover expiry behaviour."
- Ethan Ramirez (reviewer): "Estimator looks heavier than expected. Can we ensure it runs within the existing onboarding job memory constraints?"
- Maya Chen: "Reworked estimator to stream counts and use reservoir sketches; memory usage reduced from ~600MB to <120MB in integration runs. Benchmarks included in docs."
- Noah Brooks (reviewer): "CRD text templates are good; add a safeguards so drafts don't leak sensitive prompt content."
- Maya Chen: "Redacted prompt snippets by default and replaced with sanitized placeholders; team can opt into fuller context for internal release notes only."
- Priya Singh: "Approved after changes."
- Ethan Ramirez: "Approved."
- Noah Brooks: "Approved."

CI status: pass

Files changed count: 8
Additions: 620 lines
Deletions: 127 lines

Release notes (auto): "Adds an opt-in sampled affinity calibration pipeline to produce per-variant sampling vectors, and a contextual release drafter that attaches representative traces and the top performance deltas to model release drafts. Improves onboarding profile representativeness and makes changelogs more actionable for runtime and SRE teams. Backwards compatible; opt-in via onboarding flags."

Migration/rollout: "Run migration script (migrations/20241108_add_affinity_column.sql) during low-traffic window. Enable feature flag in staging for 2 weeks and compare CRD drafts with legacy changelogs. Monitor drift metrics (registry.onboard.sample_bias, release.crd.top_regressions_count)."

Notes for reviewers/ops: retain affinity vectors for 90 days by default (configurable) and rotate sample seeds monthly. If disabling SAC, the registry falls back to uniform sampling and CRD falls back to previous changelog generation path.
